Target annual 12/24 count

Screening assumes whole-episode capture and storage reset between episodes. It preserves each episode’s 12/24 compatibility count. Tank routing, partial capture and drawdown are outside this screening method.

Calendar-year discharge volume

Calendar totals split physical discharge at 1 January. Episode volumes and counts retain their counting-year attribution, so an episode crossing New Year can appear in a different year from part of its discharge.

routes.label: About
routes.text:
HB
Hydra Bench

Hydraulic evidence. Clear assessment.

Hydra Bench is a browser-based engineering workbench for reviewing exported InfoWorks ICM results, telemetry, flow surveys and rainfall data. It brings data assessment, model verification, spill analysis and scenario comparison into one place, with explicit assumptions, units and traceable source evidence. Imported engineering data is processed locally in your browser.

Open engineering method library
Your workspaces
Data / time series ↗

Upload CSV, FDV and rainfall R files, association workbooks and ICM assessment reports into a shared source pool. Assign observed, modelled and rainfall series, confirm their quantities and units, and review hydraulic traces, thresholds, rainfall events and source statistics. This is the starting point for supplying and checking the evidence used by the other workspaces.

Spills ↗

Assess observed and modelled spills using explicit thresholds, exclusions and valid temporal support. Review physical spill intervals, UK 12/24 counts and yearly or monthly comparisons. Storage assessment provides idealised storage screening and modelled spill-volume evidence to support further engineering investigation.

Network Schematic ↗

Arrange and annotate a network, assign annual spill evidence and review observed and modelled results by asset and reporting year.

Flow survey ↗

Review monitor and rain-gauge weeks from their schematics, record a rating and comment for each week, and check flow continuity in Volume balance. Monthly review brings the outcomes and actions together for PDF export.

Detriment assessment ↗

Compare baseline Scenario A with proposed Scenario B using exported ICM report evidence. The Flooding, Level and Spill tabs assess changes in flood volume, maximum water-level elevation and freeboard, or spill counts and actual durations. Explicit criteria, raw asset evidence and optional manhole / link ID lists support a focused, traceable assessment.

Verification ↗

Explore observed versus modelled agreement, depth and flow–depth rating diagnostics, and dry-weather-flow baselines. Use scatter views, fitted relationships and verification statistics to understand model performance and hydraulic behaviour, with sample support and data-validity limitations retained.

Hydraulic Calculations ↗

Assess full-flow capacity and supported turbulent normal depths for steady uniform flow in a circular pipe.

Reports ↗

Export engineering assessments and graph reports from the current analysis, and save or restore a workspace with its configuration and source fingerprints. Reports carry the relevant criteria, units and evidence so results can be reviewed and shared; saved workspaces reference the original files without embedding their raw data.

Originally created by Anzar Sajid

Created from practical hydraulic modelling and data-review workflows, Hydra Bench aims to make engineering evidence easier to inspect, compare and communicate. Its focus is on clear results, explicit assessment criteria and a streamlined path from imported data to an auditable engineering review.

HydraBench began as a local graphing and hydraulic-data review tool. It grew into an engineering decision support platform with a shared source and evidence model. Anzar Sajid directed its development with AI assistance. Third-party software and fonts retain their original authorship and licence notices.

routes.label: IT Security
routes.text:
IT Security

Version v3.0.1 · Revision ccc36427c12f003e5d9b1fee61632770b31952cc

Assessment: 2026-10-18 / single-maintainer policy; see assessment for scope and verification limits

Data processing and confidentiality

The browser application parses imported engineering files and calculates results locally using JavaScript and a Pyodide worker. Its data-confidentiality policy prohibits sending imported data, identifying metadata or derived outputs over a network.

Network connectivity

Application code, fonts and fixed runtime libraries are served from the application origin. Opening the site requires connectivity; the hosting service and network infrastructure receive ordinary asset-request information. Local file processing is distinct from resource downloading.

Data storage and retention

Selected files and calculations use browser memory and the worker virtual filesystem. Named workspaces and network layouts can persist in localStorage. Interface preferences use sessionStorage. Local data diagnostics can remove named workspace and recovery copies after confirmation. Use browser site-data controls to clear other retained origin data, and manage exported files separately.

Application security controls

The source confidentiality gate detects changes to reviewed network-capable files. Dependency files are checked against a maintained hash inventory. Browser request tests reject unapproved destinations, resource queries, request bodies and network sockets in tested flows. These checks require enforced repository checks and release rules to prevent bypass.

Software dependencies

Runtime components include Pyodide for Python execution, NumPy and pandas for analysis, Plotly for charts, SheetJS for association workbooks and Inter for typography. Their maintained inventory records versions, hashes and licence files. Dependency changes require security and compatibility review.

Security verification

Verification status is not available for this build. Release checks cover source confidentiality, dependency advisories, secrets, static analysis, engineering regression and browser requests. This is a single-maintainer project: independent human review is not available, and AI-assisted review is not a substitute. Version and source revision identify the build; consult workflow evidence for that revision.

Limitations and responsible use

Tests cover defined workflows and supported desktop browsers. Browser extensions, endpoint security and subsequent handling of exported files remain outside the application’s control. Apply your organisation’s data-handling requirements. Passing tests is not a universal security guarantee.

Security issues and reporting

Follow the security disclosure guidance. Do not place confidential datasets, credentials or sensitive evidence in public issues. Use an established private channel to the repository owner.
